newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds ended mixed to lower on Tuesday after a day in which traders focused on the new tap issue, maturing February 2007, but did little trade in it.
"The market closely watched the tap, but finally not a lot of big deals were done," one dealer said. He added most trade on the tap was done by professional players.
At 1600 GMT, the Dutch Finance Ministry announced it had raised 4.7 billion guilders under the new issue so far, a 1.1 billion guilders increase compared to yesterday.

"This bond will be the new ten-year benchmark, it's better for international (yield) comparisons, but trade in the former benchmark (the 6.00 percent January 2006) will remain active. It's a much bigger loan," one dealer said.
Dealers said trade during the day had been without any direction in particular, and could not describe possible trends.
During the day, market players had been awaiting Greenspan's testimony with some anxiety, which caused some selling pressure.
"Finally, there was not much news, but more of a relief in it. The Fed's ladies and gentlemen do watch the economy, but for the moment they don't act upon it," one dealer said.
He added he expected market relief to boost the overseas bond market, and said the Dutch one was likely to follow.
